entities.summary: Swarovski Kristallwelten in Wattens, Austria, is an art-and-garden attraction built around large installations.
entities.description: Swarovski Kristallwelten in Wattens combines large art installations with designed gardens. Visitors explore spaces made to surround them with art, making this an outing for people who enjoy visual design as well as gardens. It suits school-age children through adults; check current opening and any activity restrictions.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The large installations and gardens at Swarovski Kristallwelten in Wattens give visitors varied ways to experience art beyond looking at objects in cases.

entities.summary: Austria’s Grossglockner High Alpine Road is a 48 km mountain drive with 36 bends and a branch facing a glacier.
entities.description: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road runs from Ferleiten across the Hohe Tauern mountains through Hochtor to Heiligenblut. The 48 km journey includes the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe branch, with views towards the glacier. Its 36 bends carry you through changing mountain landscapes. The road opens seasonally, with snow and high-mountain conditions determining access.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road in Austria combines a mountain crossing, changing landscapes and glacier views in one sustained scenic drive.

entities.summary: Minimundus in Klagenfurt, Austria, pairs carefully made outdoor miniature models with an indoor area of interactive activities.
entities.description: At Minimundus in Klagenfurt, visitors explore an open-air collection of miniature models and an adjacent indoor interactive area. The workmanship rewards looking closely, while the activities add variety to the model displays. It particularly suits children aged about 4–14; check seasonal opening and activity restrictions before travel.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Minimundus in Klagenfurt is worth choosing for the detail of its miniature models and the chance to combine looking with indoor activities.

entities.summary: Kronprinzessin-Stefanie-Warte is a historic observation tower on Vienna’s Kahlenberg, with views of the city, Danube and Wienerwald forest.
entities.description: Climb the stairs of Kronprinzessin-Stefanie-Warte on Kahlenberg for a full-circle view from its 22-metre platform. The small 1887 tower adds height to a hill walk and opens views across Vienna, the Danube and surrounding forest. Volunteers operate it seasonally, so check opening before coming specifically for the climb.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The extra height of Vienna’s Kronprinzessin-Stefanie-Warte gives a Kahlenberg walk a broad city-and-forest panorama from a historic tower.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The tower visit includes climbing its interior stairs to the viewing platform.

current.note: The tower was confirmed operating in August 2026; seasonal opening applies.

entities.summary: Carinthia’s Nockalm Road is a 34 km seasonal drive through forests and rounded alpine hills between Innerkrems and Ebene Reichenau.
entities.description: Nockalm Road crosses Austria’s Nockberge Biosphere Reserve, winding through larch and Swiss-pine forest into open alpine pasture. The 34 km drive has 52 bends and two high points, including the 2,042-metre Eisentalhöhe. Its usual season runs from early May to late October, subject to mountain conditions.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Nockalm Road in Carinthia rewards drivers with a gradual change from forest to open pasture and long views across rounded alpine hills.
